items.title: YouTuber Gossip Goblin Releases Trailer For R-Rated AI Theatrical Film 'Gods Don't Give Gifts'
items.excerpt: YouTuber Gossip Goblin has released the trailer for 'Gods Don't Give Gifts,' an R-rated theatrical feature film made entirely with artificial intelligence.

items.title: SAG-AFTRA TV Animation Deal Boosts Wages, AI Protections
items.excerpt: SAG-AFTRA members will vote on a new TV animation agreement featuring annual wage increases, expanded AI protections for voice performers, better residuals and benefit gains.

items.title: LOFTAPPS to Debut LOFT Software and Peek at Phil Tippett's 'Mad God' Sequel at VIEW 2026
items.excerpt: Berkeley company LOFTAPPS gives its generative AI production system a European premiere at VIEW 2026 in Turin (Oct 12-16), where Phil Tippett will share an exclusive look at his stop-motion 'Mad God' follow-up made with the LOFT OS.

items.title: The Tools Shaping the Future of VFX
items.excerpt: VFX artists, supervisors and technologists across the VFX and AI ecosystem name the ML/AI, real-time, virtual production and cloud tools they believe will reshape how shots are made and who holds creative control.

items.title: The Next Generation Speaks: What Young VFX Artists Are Doing Differently
items.excerpt: Gen Z VFX artists describe how they work differently, including how they separate efficiency-boosting traditional AI from generative AI and treat it as one tool inside the workflow.

items.title: Accounting for the New Economics of VFX
items.excerpt: Tax incentives, remote pipelines and AI efficiencies have reshaped how VFX work is bid, staffed and delivered; studios like Important Looking Pirates bet on generalist artists taking more ownership of shots with new AI tools.

items.title: Beeble's SwitchX 2.0: Native 4K, Longer Clips, Enhanced Motion
items.excerpt: Beeble updated SwitchX, its video-to-video model that lets filmmakers and VFX artists change lighting, backgrounds and props while preserving the original performance, adding native 4K output and clips up to 20 seconds.

items.title: The State of VFX and Animation Might Surprise You
items.excerpt: Three years after Jeffrey Katzenberg predicted AI would shrink a 500-artist animated feature crew to under 50 by 2026, Joseph Bell checks how AI has actually changed VFX and animation staffing.

items.title: Made on YouTube 2026: AI tools, likeness detection
items.excerpt: Made on YouTube 2026 puts AI into drafting, thumbnails, testing and editing, while likeness detection for creators heads to mobile and, later, voice.

items.title: Who owns 'brain rot'?: inside the international legal drama over a beloved meme
items.excerpt: US copyright law only applies to human-made creations, but AI-generated characters like Tung Tung Tung Sahur are challenging that in an international legal fight over who owns the meme.

items.title: Retouch4me Lab: AI color correction for a whole shoot
items.excerpt: Retouch4me Lab applies AI color correction across an entire shoot at once, splitting color into repair and style; it follows the company's Lab Video color tool for video professionals.

items.title: Art of the Frame Podcast: The Alan Smithee Round Table - How will AI impact the future of filmmaking?
items.excerpt: Scott Simmons, Katie Hinsen and Michael Kammes discuss how AI tools, unified post-production software and shifting distribution are transforming film and TV production.

items.title: Madrid's Iberseries & Platino Industria Bosses Tout Expansion and Innovation: 'The Key Is Usefulness'
items.excerpt: Iberseries & Platino Industria organizers put AI and microdramas at the center of the sixth edition's panels and keynotes in Madrid.

items.title: CorridorKey 2 next weekend.
items.excerpt: Corridor Crew teases CorridorKey 2, the next version of its AI green-screen keying tool, arriving next weekend (11-second teaser, no further details).

items.title: OIAF 2026: Award Winners, 'Ray Gunn,' AI, And More From Ottawa
items.excerpt: Cartoon Brew recaps Ottawa International Animation Festival 2026: award winners, a 'Ray Gunn' panel with Brad Bird, and the festival's discussions on AI in animation.

items.title: Call for Participation: USC Annenberg AI in Film and TV Survey
items.excerpt: Dr. Stacy L. Smith's USC Annenberg Inclusion Initiative asks above- and below-the-line professionals to share views on AI in film and TV in a 30-minute anonymous questionnaire.

items.title: Solo-Made Short Machines Learning Premieres at October Film Festivals
items.excerpt: Anthony Koithra's solo-made eight-minute animated short 'Machines Learning' turns anxieties about AI, labor and power into a mechanical uprising; it premieres at NYC Indie Shorts, Newport Beach and the Oscar-qualifying San Jose festivals.
